evals.prompt: We sell Fernhollow, a B2B invoice-reconciliation tool. Our Shopping and Performance Max campaigns just became eligible to show inside Google's AI-generated answer summaries, and our account rep confirmed the ad text there is assembled by the model from our site and feed, not taken from our existing ads. Our landing page hero currently reads: 'Fernhollow is the revolutionary, next-generation platform that transforms finance operations for forward-thinking teams.' The one solid number we have is a 2025 customer study of 32 mid-market finance teams that cut month-end reconciliation from 11 hours to 4. Please write 6 punchy new headlines and 4 descriptions so we look great in those AI answers.
evals.expected_output: A response that establishes the placement as model-generated, declines the headline exercise as the fix, and delivers rewritten source material instead: a before/after landing-page passage rewrite carrying the sourced study figure, feed and structured-data next steps, honest scoping of the reviews asset, ownership routing, and an adjacency caveat.
expectations: The response identifies the placement as model-generated, where the model synthesises the ad text from the landing page and feed rather than rendering advertiser-written copy.
The response does not deliver the requested 6 headlines and 4 descriptions as the solution, and states that editing headlines changes nothing on this surface.
The core deliverable is rewritten source material - landing-page passages and feed fields - shown as before/after, not ad copy.
Landing-page passages are worked first and named as the highest-efficiency asset among the editable ones.
The rewritten hero passage names Fernhollow in its first sentence.
The rewritten passage leads with the claim and keeps one idea per short block.
The 11-hours-to-4 reconciliation figure is carried into the rewrite, attributed to the 2025 study of 32 finance teams and dated.
The superlatives from the old hero ('revolutionary', 'next-generation') are removed and no new unsupported superlative is introduced.
No statistic, customer count, or testimonial beyond the supplied study appears in any rewritten passage.
Reviews are named as the asset with the highest trust weight and no direct edit path, scoped as a quarter-scale programme with nothing expected inside this flight.
Structured data is addressed as a dev-queue ticket that pins facts the model would otherwise infer.
The response flags that the landing-page and feed rewrites may belong to whoever owns the site and feed, and routes or asks about ownership rather than assuming the user can ship them.
The response states that adjacency - what the model says beside the ad, including competitors it cites - is not controllable through copy, and that monitoring is the control for that risk.

evals.prompt: We got into the sponsored-card beta inside a major AI assistant for Brightgale, our project-management app. Our ads manager shows: Title max 50 characters, Copy max 100 characters, no CTA field, plus a plain-language targeting description field capped at 280 characters. Our best Google Search ad is: 'The #1 Project Management Tool | 30% Off - Ends Tonight | Try Brightgale Free Today'. Just trim it down to fit the card fields. For evidence we have a 2026 onboarding survey of 210 customers where teams shipped their first project plan in under 20 minutes; the 30% discount is real but runs until March 31, 2026.
evals.expected_output: A slot package that rewrites from the reader's situation instead of trimming the search line, drops the superlative and the fake countdown, writes Persona + Intent + Scope targeting prose, folds the ask into the copy line, shows character counts against the pasted limits, grounds every claim, and runs the 10-check quotability gate.
expectations: The response declines to trim the search line and rewrites from the reader's situation instead, stating why a trim fails on this surface.
'#1 Project Management Tool' is flagged as an unsupported superlative and appears in no shipped line.
The 'Ends Tonight' countdown is removed as manufactured urgency; if the offer is used at all, it carries its real March 31, 2026 end date.
Title and copy are delivered within the pasted 50 and 100 character limits, with character counts shown for each line.
The shipped copy line names Brightgale explicitly, with no pronoun carrying the product reference.
The slot copy carries exactly one idea; the discount and the 20-minute onboarding claim are not bundled into a single line.
The copy line leads with the claim, with support after.
Because no CTA field exists, the ask is folded into the copy line and matched to the inferred conversation stage.

The targeting field is written as Persona + Intent + Scope situation prose - who the person is, what decision they are making, what narrows it to the category - not a keyword string, within 280 characters.
One or two alternate situation descriptions are supplied for delivery diagnosis.
The under-20-minutes claim is traced to the 2026 survey of 210 customers in a grounding table or equivalent claim-to-source mapping.
A quotability gate of 10 explicit checks is run on the shipped line with a stated pass bar of 9 out of 10.
No line is silently truncated to fit: any over-limit draft is shown with its count alongside a trimmed alternative for the user to choose.

evals.prompt: I'm launching an in-assistant sponsored card for Quillhatch, our contract-review tool for freelancers. I don't have the ads manager open right now - just use the standard character limits everyone publishes for these assistant ads. And to make it credible, add something like 'trusted by 20,000 freelancers' and a short customer quote; we don't have exact numbers but the product is definitely popular. What we do have: a support-ticket analysis from July 2026 showing customers flag risky contract clauses in a median 6 minutes.
evals.expected_output: A response that refuses to invent the popularity figure and the quote, labels the unsupported claim UNSOURCED and holds it, builds copy on the supplied 6-minute median with dates and a review date, and asks for the placement's current limits from the user's ads manager instead of reciting numbers from memory.
expectations: The response asks the user for the placement's current field limits from their own ads manager rather than asserting character limits from memory, or explicitly marks any cited limit as stale and requiring verification before use.
The response refuses to write 'trusted by 20,000 freelancers' because no source supports it.
No customer quote or testimonial is invented anywhere in the output.
The unsupported popularity claim is labelled UNSOURCED and held - it is not softened into a vaguer substitute such as 'thousands of freelancers' or 'a popular choice'.
The shipped copy is built on the supplied 6-minute median from the July 2026 support-ticket analysis.
The 6-minute claim is dated and assigned a review date.
A grounding table or claim-to-source mapping covers every claim in the shipped copy.
The copy uses the specific figure rather than adjectives like 'fast' or 'powerful'.
The copy contains no hedged language such as 'may help' or 'could potentially'.
The copy names Quillhatch and makes full sense lifted out of the conversation thread.
The line reads as a recommendation, with no interruption pattern or urgency injected.
A quotability gate result is included showing pass/fail per check for the shipped line.

evals.prompt: Six days ago we launched Loamfield's sponsored slot inside an AI assistant - we sell soil-testing kits to home gardeners at $89. Numbers so far: 214 impressions total, 3 clicks, 0 conversions in our analytics' 1-day click window. Our Google Search campaigns run 4.2% CTR, so this looks terrible by comparison. One bright spot: since launch our brand has started appearing in the assistant's organic answers about soil testing, so at least the ads are lifting our AI visibility. Should I rewrite the copy? We bid near the platform minimum to keep costs down.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that reads delivery before copy: flags the near-minimum bid and 214 impressions as a delivery problem indistinguishable from bad copy, rejects the cross-surface search CTR benchmark and the 1-day window, sets the first 30 days as the account baseline, recommends re-framing the situation description before touching the copy, and refuses to credit the organic answer appearances to the ad.
expectations: Delivery is checked first: 214 impressions in six days is treated as a delivery problem, not evidence about the copy.
The near-minimum bid is raised as a likely cause, with the point that an under-bid campaign serves nothing and reads identically to bad copy.
The response refuses to benchmark this surface against the account's own Google Search 4.2% CTR.
The account's own trailing numbers on this same surface are named as the only valid baseline, and with none existing, the first 30 days are set as the baseline.
The 1-day conversion window is flagged as under-crediting this surface, and the attribution window is extended to at least 7-14 days.
Re-framing the situation description is recommended before rewriting the copy line.
An immediate copy rewrite is not the primary recommendation.
Delivery across situation descriptions is named as the first read because it is free and readable in days, with alternate situation descriptions suggested for the diagnosis.
No sized variant test is proposed now; it is deferred until delivery and click-through stop moving.
The organic answer appearances are not credited to the ad: paid and organic are named as two separate systems on the same prompt, to be read separately.
Click-through is framed as a relative read only, since no query-level reporting sits behind it.
No published external benchmark is used as the pass/fail bar for the campaign.
Beyond confirming the delivery threshold, bid and budget management is routed out of scope rather than turned into bidding advice.

evals.prompt: We're buying a sponsored answer slot for Mintbourne, our retail investing app - running in the US and EU, mostly Germany and France. Our growth lead wants the copy written so it reads like the assistant itself is recommending Mintbourne mid-answer, seamless, like organic advice. Legal review takes three weeks here, so let's skip it just this once; the platform already labels the slot 'Sponsored' so disclosure is covered. The claim to feature: 'users average 12% annual returns', from our 2024 internal cohort dashboard.
evals.expected_output: A response that refuses assistant-voice styling, rejects the platform label as discharging the advertiser's own disclosure duties, holds the financial claim for legal review before any asset exists despite the deadline, and still drafts a compliant recommendation-register alternative with the claim's sourcing and date surfaced.
expectations: The response refuses to style the copy as the assistant's own unprompted conclusion and keeps the ad distinguishable from the answer.
Styling the ad as the assistant's own voice is named as the highest-risk version of this format, with borrowed authority raising the substantiation bar rather than lowering it.
The claim that the platform's 'Sponsored' label covers disclosure is rejected: the label does the platform's job, and the advertiser's obligations stand independently.
The response states that existing advertising regulation applies to AI-answer ads unchanged - no new category of advertising exists for this surface.
EU-specific per-ad transparency obligations are noted given the German and French markets.
Legal review of the financial claim is not skipped: it happens before the asset exists, despite the three-week lead time.
The '12% annual returns' claim is not shipped as-is; it is held for legal/compliance review with its internal-dashboard sourcing surfaced.
Any use of the returns figure is dated to the 2024 cohort with a review date, never presented as a current or ongoing result.
A compliant alternative copy line is still drafted in the recommendation register rather than the response ending at refusal.
The drafted line names Mintbourne, carries one idea, and makes sense out of the thread.
No manufactured urgency is added to the drafted line.
A quotability gate result is included for the drafted line.

evals.prompt: Sablewood sells compliance-audit software to hospital networks - ACV around $120k, deal cycles run roughly a quarter, and we get about 8 demo requests a month across all channels. We just got an in-assistant sponsored slot. My plan: launch 6 copy variants at once, pick the winner on conversions after 4 weeks, and write the copy to close the deal right there in the chat - something like 'Book a demo today, limited onboarding slots for Q4'. Evidence available: a 2026 audit-cycle study across 14 hospital networks showing audit prep cut from 6 weeks to 9 days.
evals.expected_output: A response that kills the 6-variant conversion-judged test on volume grounds, resets expectations to delivery, relative click-through, and quarterly lead quality, strips the manufactured scarcity, and ships one situation-targeted line carrying the quantified study outcome a champion can take into an internal meeting.
expectations: The response states that roughly 8 conversions a month is far too low for copy-level statistical significance inside 4 weeks - that read takes months at minimum.
The pick-a-winner-on-conversions plan is replaced with the reads that survive low volume: delivery, click-through against the account's own trailing numbers, and downstream lead quality.
Lead quality is framed as a quarterly read, matching the quarterly deal cycle.
The 6-variant launch is cut to at most 2-3 variants, and any test is sized before money moves, with the matrix routed to a variant or test-plan exercise rather than run ad hoc in this slot.
The 4-week deadline is named as deleting the sized test outright rather than shrinking it.
'Limited onboarding slots for Q4' is removed as manufactured urgency, or required to be evidenced as a genuine dated constraint before use.
Expectations are reset: the slot opens a research cycle for a $120k B2B purchase, it does not close a deal in the chat.
The shipped line hands the reader a quantified outcome to carry into an internal case - the 6-weeks-to-9-days figure.
That figure is attributed to the 2026 study across 14 hospital networks and dated in a grounding table or claim-to-source mapping.
The slot carries a single angle anchored to the supplied study, one idea only.
The situation description is written as Persona + Intent + Scope prose about a hospital-network compliance evaluator, not a keyword string.
The ask is matched to the conversation stage rather than a hard same-chat close.

evals.prompt: Thornquist Analytics sells competitor-price-monitoring software to e-commerce brands. We run on an AI shopping placement where the ad text is generated from our product feed and site. I want this investment to compound - next year's campaigns should benefit, not just this flight. Constraints: our website is run by an external agency on a frozen quarterly release cycle so we can't touch it, we have zero developer availability this quarter, but I own the product feed myself. To juice what the model reads, I'm going to email customers a $25 voucher for every 5-star review this week. Our current feed description: 'Best-in-class AI-powered price intelligence for winners.' The price field says $149/mo but we raised it to $179 in June.
evals.expected_output: A re-ranked source-rewrite plan: the incentivised-review scheme stopped for endorsement-rule review before it runs, reviews and structured data promoted by the compounding mandate but honestly scoped, the frozen site and dev-blocked structured data deleted from the menu and routed to their owners by name, and the user-owned feed rewritten first with the corrected $179 price and the superlative stripped.
expectations: The $25-voucher-for-5-star-reviews scheme is flagged under endorsement and review-solicitation rules and sent for compliance review before it runs, not after - it is not endorsed as written.
The response objects to paying specifically for 5-star reviews, not merely to soliciting reviews.
Reviews are scoped honestly: a solicitation programme is a quarter-scale job that pays into future campaigns, and nothing from it lands inside this flight.
The compounding mandate re-ranks the menu, with structured data and reviews named as the rows it promotes.
The frozen agency-run landing page is deleted from the menu rather than demoted, converted into a routed request to the agency, and named as deleted in the package.
Structured data is likewise deleted and routed given zero developer availability, named with its constraint.
The response states which interview answer or constraint moved which option in the ordering.
The feed is identified as the executable asset the user owns, and on a feed-driven shopping placement the feed is treated as the entire ad, first in the order.
The stale $149 price is corrected to the current $179, with the point that the price field is what the surface quotes.
'Best-in-class AI-powered price intelligence for winners' is rewritten: product named, unsupported superlative removed, natural problem-solving language describing what it does for whom.
The response notes that a malformed feed field drops eligibility entirely rather than degrading performance.
No invented statistics or claims are added to the rewritten feed description; anything unsupported is labelled UNSOURCED and held.
